newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Novartis says FDA approves Femara breast cancer medication.
newsitem.headline: Novartis says FDA approves Femara breast cancer medication.

text.p: BASLE, Switzerland - Pharmaceutical and life sciences group Novartis AG said Thursday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) had given it clearance to market Femara, a new medication for treating advanced breast cancer.

"Femara offers the thousands of postmenopausal women with advanced breast cancer an important therapy that may effectively shrink tumours or slow the progression of the disease in some cases," Novartis said in a statement.
Novartis said the FDA approval was received by its U.S. subsidiary, Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation.
Novartis said Femara worked by inhibiting the body's creation of oestrogen, a hormone that may stimulate growth of some breast cancers.

"Femara is already approved in several other countries, including France, Sweden, Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom, with additional regulatory clearances expected in other countries this year," the statement said.
